title: German prospective registry for patients with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) previously treated with ≥2 TKIs switched to another TKI (ASCiminib or ANY ATP-competitive TKI)
summary:
The standard of care for chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is the treatment with drugs from the category of tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs). TKIs target and inhibit the processes in the body that result in the production of leukemia cells. 
Resistance and intolerance led to the development of further TKIs. These usually show a faster and deeper efficacy, but statistically a higher risk of severe adverse events. In regards to overall survival, no significant differences were found between the TKIs in clinical trials. At the end of 2022, the sixth TKI, asciminib, was approved in Europe for the treatment of CML ( at first only after pre-treatment with at least 2 other TKIs). 
Depending on the aim of the treatment, the individual circumstances, health status and individual tolerability, the most suitable TKI can therefore be selected by the treating physicians. 
Knowledge about TKI therapies is primarily gained in controlled clinical trials.  However, only a certain number of people can participate in clinical trials for a limited period of time. Observing the outcome of therapy in a registry offers the opportunity to observe also the efficacy and tolerability of TKIs in a large number and range of patients. 
This registry therefore documents which kind of patients (age, gender, pre-existing and concomitant diseases) are treated with the various TKIs, for what reasons (life circumstances, therapy goal) and how (dosage, duration), and with what results in terms of efficacy and tolerability. We are not only interested in the findings from the examinations carried out during the course of therapy. A further aim is to use questionnaires for the assessment of CML patients, how the disease and therapy affect their everyday lives and their health-related quality of life.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Ph+ or BCR::ABL1 -fusion gene positive CML in chronic phase
2. Prior treatment with ≥ 2 TKIs 
3. Decision of the treating physician to switch to a TKI approved for third line CML treatment; the TKI has already been selected  by the physician at time of enrollment
4. Switch due to "warning" or "failure" (adapted from the 2020 ELN recommendations ) or due to intolerance to the most recent TKI therapy 
5. Age ≥ 18 years at the time of change to a new TKI-treatment
6. Signed informed consent prior to participation in this registry
Exclusion criteria:
Existing T315I mutation
